question.text: For G-Sec cash-settled Interest Rate Derivatives, position limits at the client, trading member, and exchange/market-wide levels are typically specified by reference to which of the following?

answer.text: Open interest in the contract and the relevant maturity bucket, subject to an exchange-level overall cap on the outstanding stock of the underlying bond
A fixed rupee amount applicable uniformly across all clients, trading members, and the market as a whole
The trading member's paid-up share capital alone, with no reference to open interest or maturity
The free-float market capitalisation of the issuer, with no maturity-bucket differentiation

explanation.text: The Logic: For G-Sec cash-settled IRD, position limits at the client and trading-member level are framed in terms of open interest in the contract, with separate calibrations for different maturity buckets. Above that, an exchange-level overall cap (a percentage of the outstanding stock of the underlying bond) caps the aggregate market-wide exposure. This structure ties allowed positions to actual contract liquidity while still preventing any one product from getting too large relative to the underlying bond. The Trap: A single fixed rupee amount applied uniformly across all levels would ignore both contract liquidity and the size of the underlying bond. Paid-up share capital governs membership eligibility, not position limits. Free-float market capitalisation is an equity-segment concept and does not drive G-Sec IRD limits. Note: The cited workbook (NISM Series IV, pages 234-237) defines position limits for G-Sec cash-settled IRD in terms of open interest and maturity bucket plus an exchange-level cap on outstanding underlying bond, but does not contain the simple "market-wide = 15% of outstanding stock / TM = lower of 15% of market-wide or Rs. 1,000 crore / client = Rs. 500 crore" formula that the original numeric version of this item relied on. The framing above mirrors the structural description in the workbook without claiming specific numeric values.
